newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Monitors rescued in Albania restaurant siege.
newsitem.headline: Monitors rescued in Albania restaurant siege.

text.p: Romanian troops working with multinational forces in Girokaster, southern Albania, rescued 11 shaken foreign election monitoring staff trapped by armed gangs in a restaurant on Wednesday, officials here said.

Tony Welch, Albanian-based head of an Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission in Albania to oversee the planned June 29 poll, said troops moved in after men with Kalashnikov rifles demanded money from the foreigners.

"They're alright," he told Reuters, referring to the OSCE observer group including a Swiss and a Dutchman. It was not yet clear if any of the observers would opt to leave this Balkan country as tensions mount ahead of the poll, he added.

The OSCE, in Albania to help with and monitor elections called after rioting and unrest earlier this year, has voiced grave concerns about the security of its observers as the country heads to vote with parts still under gang rule.

Welch said the four observer teams accompanied by three Albanian staff were sitting on the terrace of the restaurant when the armed men approached. Another group appeared later and eventually about 15 armed people were blocking the exit.

He said communication problems meant the observers, who retreated inside, had to wait about an hour before troops from a 6,500-strong multinational protection force arrived, apparently instantly dispersing the gangs.

The observers, among advance parties sent to prepare for hundreds of foreigners who will monitor Albania's parliamentary elections, were finally returned safely to base aboard armoured personnel carriers, Welch said.
